content.thinking:
I need to work through the first question involving the root तप् (दिवादि, meaning ऐश्वर्ये, आत्मनेपदी, अनिट्), building up उप + तप् with यङ् then णिच् then सन्, targeting लुट् कर्तरि परस्मैपद मध्यमपुरुष एकवचन. I'm deriving the यङन्त form तातप्यते through reduplication.

Now I'm working through how णिच् attaches to the यङन्त stem तातप्य — applying यस्य हलः to drop the य, then checking whether the resulting अ-lopa and उपधा-वृद्धि interact via स्थानिवद्भाव rules, comparing against the known pattern for बोभूय+णिच्.

Checking similar forms like बोभूययति confirms the pattern for वोबल् roots ending in vowels versus हल्-ending roots like पापचयति, where स्थानिवद्भाव of the अ-लोप preserves the non-वृद्धि shape. This supports going with तातपि, though I want to verify the rule ordering for यस्य हलः (6.4.49) applying to यङ्'s य.

Looking at Kashika's gloss on this sutra, there's the question of whether "यस्य" indicates deletion of the whole संघात (य् + अ) rather than just the य्, which matters for whether स्थानिवद्भाव applies afterward.

Right, so I recall the actual commentary now: "आदेः परस्य" restricts the deletion to just the य् (the first letter of the संघात), then "अतो लोपः" separately deletes the अ, and its स्थानिवद्भाव blocks गुण। So the conclusion holds either way — तातपि with no वृद्धि, confirming बेभिदिता as the correct form.

Now turning to सन् with तातपि: since तातपि is अनेकाच्, the अनिट् rule for तप् (एकाच् उपदेश अनुदात्त) doesn't apply here, so इट् is added — giving तातपयिष्। I'm working out the reduplication for सन् on this base, considering which एकाच् portion undergoes द्वित्व.

I'm trying to recall the precedent for यङ्+सन् reduplication, like बोभूयिषते, to figure out whether dvitva applies again here or whether the existing यङ् reduplication suffices without further doubling.

I'm trying to recall the Mahabhashya/Kashika discussion on why यङन्त + सन् doesn't get doubly reduplicated: with "पापच्य + सन्", the root पापच्य's first एकाच् is "पा", so another reduplication would theoretically yield "पपापच्यिषते" — but this doesn't seem right, so there must be some governing principle preventing it that I'm not recalling precisely.

I'm now trying a different angle, recalling जागृ as a lexically reduplicated root (counted among अभ्यस्त roots like जक्षित्यादि), and how सन् applied to it still produces further reduplication as जिजागरिषति — suggesting that lexical reduplication doesn't automatically block सन्-reduplication, which cuts against my earlier reasoning about यङन्त roots.

Actually there might be a specific exemption: "अनभ्यासस्य" carried forward from 6.1.8 into 6.1.9 could mean the reduplication rule for सन् applies only to a non-reduplicated base, exempting यङन्त roots from further reduplication when सन् is added. That would explain why बोभूयिषते doesn't get doubly reduplicated.

I'm trying to recall whether यङन्त forms get reduplicated again before सन् or लिट्, since जागृ lacks a technical अभ्यास (so it reduplicates), while यङन्त already carries one by rule 6.1.4, meaning अनभ्यासस्य would block further reduplication there.

I need to think through whether "अनभ्यासस्य" qualifies the root itself or the first एकाच् of it — the Kashika phrasing "धातोरनभ्यासस्य...एकाचः" suggests both words describe the root as lacking an existing अभ्यास, so if the root already has an abhyāsa (like "तातपि"), reduplication is blocked entirely.

I'm trying to recall the actual Kashika example illustrating this — something involving यङ्लुगन्त roots in लिट्, like बोभूव, where the root already shows reduplication from यङ्, so लिट् doesn't reduplicate it again.

Maybe I should consider whether these question sets were generated by a computational system like Vidyut-prakriya, which implements these dvitva rules programmatically. I'm trying to recall how such an engine would handle यङ्+णिच्+सन् formations and whether it checks the "anabhyāsasya" condition explicitly when an abhyāsa already exists from a prior process. I should instead look for known grammatical or literary examples of this combination to ground my reasoning.

Let me reconsider the alternative parsing of "धातोरनभ्यासस्य" — treating it as "of the dhātu, the non-abhyāsa part" instead — but that leads to an odd reduplication result like "तातितपयिष," which doesn't seem right either. I'm also trying to recall whether SK's णिजन्त examples, like "औणिणत्" under ओणृ, shed light on how सन् interacts with चङ् here, but nothing fits cleanly yet.

I'm trying to recall the precise Siddhanta Kaumudi gloss on sutra 6.1.8, specifically what qualifies as "anabhyāsa" (non-reduplicated) and the exception clause distinguishing the first versus second vowel-doubling in liṭ forms, but the exact counter-example escapes me.

I'm wondering whether the point is about avoiding re-reduplication where the śluk rule already applies, like in juhoti-class verbs in liṭ, or in yaṅluganta forms such as "bobhūva" where cvi-type doubling (carkarīta) comes into play.

Then I recall the actual Mahābhāṣya example better: it's about desiderative-within-desiderative, like "jugupsiṣate" from gup — first getting jugupsate (ātmanepada denominative-like formation), then adding san again, which is where the anabhyāsasya restriction on sanyaṅ becomes relevant.

For तातपयिष, no reduplication applies here since it's already past that stage — सन् just takes इट् because of the अनेकाच् rule, giving तातपयिष, and with उप it's उपतातपयिष.

Checking परस्मैपद for लुट् मध्यम एकवचन: तातपयिष + तास् + सि with इट् insertion gives तातपयिषितासि, and with उप, उपतातपयिषितासि — though I'm now second-guessing whether तप् दिवादि actually permits परस्मैपद here.

So the तप् root is आत्मनेपदी in दिवादि, but णिच् makes it उभयपदी, and सन् following follows पूर्ववत् rules treating the णिजन्त base, so परस्मैपद should still hold. I'll go with उपतातपयिषितासि as the answer, and the गण detail about तप् ऐश्वर्ये doesn't change this outcome. Now I should verify whether यङ् can even apply to तप् given it requires an एकाच् हलादि root.

For the second question, I'm working through वुगिँ in भ्वादि with meaning वर्जने — it's इदित्, so नुम् augment gives वुङ्ग्, a परस्मैपदी root. With उपसर्ग अभि, applying यङ् then णिच् in लुङ् परस्मैपद मध्यम द्विवचन, I form the reduplication: अभ्यास वु takes गुण to become वो by 7.4.82, giving वोवुङ्ग्य, and I still need to check where नुम् applies for इदित् roots in this derivation.

Adding the णिच् affix next, I'm checking whether उपधा गुण applies — since the उपधा here is the consonant ङ् rather than a vowel, पुगन्तलघूपधस्य गुणः doesn't trigger, so the form stays as वोवुङ्ग् without additional guna.

For लुङ्, I'm working through चङ् formation with णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः कर्तरि चङ्, attaching मध्यमपुरुष द्विवचन तम्, and applying णेरनिटि to delete the णि, leaving वोवुङ्ग्+अ. Since reduplication already exists (अनभ्यासस्य blocks further reduplication) and the उपधा ह्रस्व rule under णौ चङ्यु doesn't apply to a consonant उपधा, I'm now checking the augment rules next.

Adding the अट् augment gives अवोवुङ्गत, and with तम् attached, अवोवुङ्गतम्. I'm double-checking whether चङ् reduplication really stays blocked for this यङन्त-णिजन्त case by comparing to similar forms like अबोभूयत् — I believe the अनभ्यासस्य anuवृत्ति through 6.1.8 to 6.1.11 confirms it's blocked, so this form holds. Adding अभि gives अभ्यवोवुङ्गतम्. Now I'm moving to Question 3, looking at गल्हँ in कुत्सायाम् sense, भ्वादि आत्मनेपदी.

For this root, I'm working out the यङ् formation in लुङ् परस्मैपद प्रथम बहुवचन with the उपसर्ग वि, building up the reduplicated stem गल्ह् → ग → ज (via कुहोश्चुः) → जा (दीर्घोऽकितः), checking whether रीगृदुपधस्य applies since गल्ह् has ल्ह् as उपध rather than ऋ, and considering whether the ऋकार-ल convention extends coverage to this root.

Since the उपधा is the consonant ल्, not ऌ, that rule doesn't apply, giving जागल्ह्य. Adding णिच् with इ gives जागल्हि since there's no वृद्धि (उपधा being a consonant rather than अ), and now I'm forming the लुङ् चङ् स्वरूप before adding the तिङ् ending.

For झि, I need to check whether जागल्ह् counts as अभ्यस्त, since झेर्जुस् would replace झि with जुस् in that case — otherwise it goes through the normal अन्ति → अन् path with अट् and वि prefixed to get व्यजागल्हन्.

So the answer is व्यजागल्हन् for that form, matching the standard अचीकरन् pattern rather than अचीकरुः. Moving to question 4, I need to work out टुक्षु (अदादि, क्षु शब्दे) with नि उपसर्ग, building यङ् then णिच् then सन्, लिट्, परस्मैपद उत्तम बहुवचन — starting with the सार्वधातुक दीर्घ giving क्षू and then working out the reduplication via हलादिः शेषः.

Applying शर्पूर्वाः खयः carefully, since क् precedes ष् rather than the reverse, हलादिः शेषः keeps क् in the अभ्यास. Then shortening to कु, applying कुहोश्चुः to get चु, and finally गुण giving चो — leading toward चोक्षूय as the यङ् stem, resolving the order of द्वित्व versus दीर्घ to arrive at this result.

Working out the णिच् form, since अतो लोपः removes the अ but यस्य हलः doesn't apply because य् follows ऊ (not a हल्), the य stays, giving चोक्षूयि. I check whether उपधा गुण applies here — since the उपधा is already a गुरु long ऊ, no लघूपध guna is needed, and there's no वृद्धि triggered at the final य्, so चोक्षूयि stands as the form.

Now building the सन्नन्त: चोक्षूयि + सन् takes इट् since it's अनेकाच्, giving गुण of the णि-vowel — चोक्षूये + इष् → चोक्षूययिष्, with no reduplication since अनभ्यासस्य applies to such long derived stems.

For the लिट् form of this सन्नन्त, I'm working through whether आम्-प्रत्यय applies per 3.1.35, since the rule covers roots formed with a प्रत्यय (sanādyanta), and सन्नन्त counts as such — so this अनेकाच् root should take आम् rather than direct लिट् endings.

After adding आम् (with अतो लोपः giving चोक्षूययिषाम्), I need कृ/भू/अस् as अनुप्रयोग in लिट् to carry the actual personal ending, since आम्-forms are periphrastic. I'm leaning toward कृ as the conventional choice, checking 1.3.63 to confirm it can take परस्मैपद here since the base is उभयपदी. For उत्तम पुरुष बहुवचन परस्मैपद, the ending is मस् → म, and कृ reduplicates to चकृ before adding म with the required इट्.

Checking the क्रादिनियम list (कृसृभृवृस्तुद्रुस्रुश्रुवो लिटि), I see कृ is explicitly excluded from taking इट् here, so the form is simply चकृम — giving चोक्षूययिषाञ्चकृम् (or with नि-उपसर्ग, निचोक्षूययिषाञ्चकृम्), and I confirm there's no नत्व issue and the षत्व of सन् after इ is correctly applied.

For बहुत (तप् + यङ्), I verify तातप्यते is valid per the यङ् rule (धातोरेकाचो हलादेः क्रियासमभिहारे यङ्), and since तातपि + सन् has no actual reduplication triggered by सन् itself, सन्यतः (7.4.79) doesn't apply — matching the pattern seen in जुगुप्सिषते and मीमांसिषते, confirming no further reduplication is needed.

Moving to the luṭ form, I work out तातपयिषितासि, giving उपतातपयिषितासि with the उप prefix. Then for वुगिँ, I derive the नुम्-infixed and परसवर्ण form वुङ्ग्, apply यङ् reduplication with हलादिः शेष to get अभ्यास वु, then गुण to वो, building toward वोवुङ्ग्...

Continuing to णिच् and चङ्, I arrive at अवोवुङ्गतम्, checking whether 7.4.1's उपधा rule applies, then combine with अभि via इको यणचि to get अभ्यवोवुङ्गतम्. For Q3, वि + अजागल्हन् sandhis to व्यजागल्हन्. For Q4, I'm working out निचोक्षूययिषाञ्चकृम, deciding between ञ्च and ंच spelling.
